
ENGINE VIEW  (grafts — mounts in the ENGINE's derived mount namespace, NOT the
  payload's. The payload cannot see any of these; no profile can ask for one.)
  graft-ro    /home/u/proj/sub/elsewhere-graft              (snug)
            from /usr
            asked /home/u/proj/sub/elsewhere-link
            resolved: the path snug's own code named is a SYMLINK on the host;
            snug resolved it before judging G4 and grafts the resolved path
            above. A source under any path the payload can write is a path the
            payload chooses, so this is the row to read twice
            abuse: a container given this graft reads the host tree a symlink
            the payload planted resolves to, not the literal path snug's own
            code named
            note: this graft's destination is inside a writable bind of a host
            directory (/home/u/proj/sub) — the payload can create and write
            there directly, and any write on this path reaches the HOST and
            persists after the sandbox exits.
  graft-ro    /home/u/proj/sub/ro-graft                     (snug)
            from /home/u/proj/sub/ro-src
            abuse: a container given a read-only bind of this can still
            enumerate everything under the host tree it names, even though it
            cannot write to it
            note: this graft's destination is inside a writable bind of a host
            directory (/home/u/proj/sub) — the payload can create and write
            there directly, and any write on this path reaches the HOST and
            persists after the sandbox exits.
  graft-rw    /home/u/proj/sub/rw-graft                     (snug)
            from /home/u/proj/sub/rw-src
            abuse: a container that is given a bind of this writes to the host
            tree directly, so a file it creates is visible to every later
            process that reads the same host path
            note: this graft's destination is inside a writable bind of a host
            directory (/home/u/proj/sub) — the payload can create and write
            there directly, and any write on this path reaches the HOST and
            persists after the sandbox exits.
